summary: Training reference for the Revibe warranty claim process, from the 3-page PDF "8.1 Warranties - Issues (Seller & KAMs)". The pack has no narration or transcript lines, so every fact is cited to a PDF page image (kind "page"). Page 1 is the overview, page 2 is the seller decision (Valid/Invalid), and page 3 covers Revibe Care+ paid repairs. Items marked unclear need a KAM to confirm before relying on them.

steps.screen: Revibe Warranty Process (workflow 1/3, overview)
steps.action: Customer raises the warranty claim in the My Account section on Revibe; status Pending, Revibe team to review. Card is labelled NO ACTION REQUIRED.

evidence.quote: The customer raises a warranty claim through the “My Account” section on Revibe. Status: Pending (Revibe team to review)

steps.screen: Revibe Warranty Process (overview)
steps.action: Revibe agent checks the claim info. Missing documents are requested from the customer; if not provided, the claim is Cancelled. Once complete, the repair supplier is assigned; status Pending Collection.

evidence.quote: The agent checks the claim info. Missing documents → requested from the customer; not provided → Cancelled. Once complete, the repair supplier is assigned. Status: Pending Collection

steps.screen: Revibe Warranty Process (overview)
steps.action: Pickup: for AE and ZA the AWB is auto-created and the claim moves to Under Collection immediately. For SA the seller creates the AWB manually. Once picked up from the customer, the claim goes In Transit.

evidence.quote: AE & ZA: AWB auto-created — moves to Under Collection immediately. SA: Seller to create the AWB manually. Once picked up from the customer → In Transit

steps.screen: Revibe Warranty Process (overview)
steps.action: Seller action: once the courier delivers the device, the seller sees the claim with status Under QC and marks it Valid or Invalid.

evidence.quote: Once the Courier Company delivers the seller can see the claim which status becomes Under QC. Two options: Mark VALID / Mark INVALID

steps.screen: Revibe Warranty Process (overview, routing box)
steps.action: If the pickup fails (customer does not hand over the device): status Collection failed; the agent asks the customer if they want a new AWB. Yes: new AWB (auto for AE and ZA, manual by the seller for SA) and the claim is Under collection again. No: Cancelled.

evidence.quote: Collection failed — the customer doesn't hand over the device. Agent asks the customer if they want a new AWB. Yes → new AWB (auto for AE & ZA · manual by the seller for SA) → Under collection again. No → Cancelled

steps.screen: Revibe Warranty Process (overview, routing box)
steps.action: Pick the repair supplier: within 1 year with no misuse declared, the original seller repairs (see page 2). After 1 year, or when the customer declares misuse, the Revibe Repair Partner (Revibe Care+) repairs, and the original seller does not see the claim (see page 3).

evidence.quote: Within 1 year, no misuse declared. The seller inspects the device and identifies the issue (page 2). / After 1 year, or the customer declares misuse. The original seller doesn't see the claim (page 3).

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC (workflow 2/3)
steps.action: Within 1 year, the seller inspects the device and marks the claim Valid (repair it) or Invalid (reason + proof). Revibe reviews every Invalid claim.

evidence.quote: Within 1 year: the seller inspects the device and marks the claim Valid (repair it) or Invalid (reason + proof). Revibe reviews every Invalid claim.

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, VALID column
steps.action: Valid path: seller repairs the device; in the portal the seller clicks “Repair finished” after Under repair; the claim then goes Ship back under collection, Shipped back, Delivered. Final output: the seller fixes the device and ships it back to the customer.

evidence.quote: Under repair → seller clicks “Repair finished” → Ship back under collection → Shipped back → Delivered

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, VALID column
steps.action: Ship-back cost: SA seller creates and pays the AWB; AE and ZA AWB by Revibe with 30 AED deducted from the seller.

evidence.quote: SA: seller creates and pays the AWB. AE & ZA: AWB by Revibe · 30 AED deducted from the seller

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, VALID column
steps.action: Delivery failed on ship-back: the customer refuses delivery and the claim shows Delivery failed. The agent asks if the customer wants a new attempt. Yes: seller pays a new AWB and the claim returns to Ship back under collection. No: Device disposed.

evidence.quote: The customer refuses the delivery → Delivery failed. Agent asks if the customer wants a new attempt: Yes → seller pays a new AWB → Ship back under collection. No → Device disposed

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, INVALID column
steps.action: Invalid path step 1: the seller submits proof. Reason and proof of invalidity are required; the claim becomes Invalid claim.

evidence.quote: Seller submits proof. Reason + proof of invalidity required → Invalid claim

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, INVALID column
steps.action: Invalid path step 2: Revibe agent review. If the agent agrees, the device is sent to the Lab. If the agent challenges, the agent marks the claim Valid with a rationale. If the seller must cover, the claim goes Under revision and the seller marks Valid or Invalid again, then the agent reviews again (Invalid goes to Lab). If the misuse is declared but the customer has RC+, the seller gives a quotation (page 3).

evidence.quote: Agrees → device sent to the Lab. Challenges → marks Valid with a rationale: Seller must cover → Under revision → seller marks Valid / Invalid again → agent reviews again (Invalid → Lab). Misuse but customer has RC+ → seller quotation (page 3)

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, INVALID column, lab collection (AE only)
steps.action: Lab collection (AE only): a Quiqup AWB is auto-created and the seller hands the device to Quiqup. The claim then goes Pending lab collection, In transit to lab, Lab under QC.

evidence.quote: Lab collection (AE only). Pending lab collection. Quiqup AWB auto-created · seller hands the device to Quiqup → In transit to lab → Lab under QC

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, INVALID column, lab final decision
steps.action: Lab final decision. If Lab Valid: customer refunded, then Pending lab to seller collection, In transit lab to seller, Delivered to seller. If Lab Invalid: Invalid claim confirmed, claim closed; AE Revibe ships the device back; ZA and SA the customer pays the shipping fees (Stripe code entered once paid), 90 days to pay; then Ship back under collection, Shipped back, Delivered; or Delivery failed (new attempt, or Device disposed).

evidence.quote: Lab Valid → customer refunded. Pending lab to seller collection → In transit lab to seller → Delivered to seller. Lab Invalid → Invalid claim confirmed — claim closed. AE: Revibe ships the device back. ZA & SA: the customer pays the shipping fees (Stripe code entered once paid) · 90 days to pay

steps.screen: Seller Decision · Under QC, OUTSIDE AE box
steps.action: Outside AE there is no Lab: the agent's confirmation of the seller's Invalid is final.

evidence.quote: OUTSIDE AE. No Lab yet: the agent's confirmation of the seller's Invalid is final.

steps.screen: Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs (workflow 3/3), Route A
steps.action: Route A (within 1 year, original seller finds misuse): the seller marks Invalid (misuse). The agent sees the customer has RC+ and marks “Misuse but customer has RC+”. The original seller then gives a quotation and repairs the device; Revibe covers the cost.

evidence.quote: The seller marks Invalid (misuse). The agent sees that the customer has RC+ and marks “Misuse but customer has RC+”. The original seller then gives a quotation and repairs the device — Revibe covers the cost.

steps.screen: Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs, Route B
steps.action: Route B (after 1 year, or misuse declared): the device goes straight to the Revibe Repair Partner; the original seller does not see the claim. The partner inspects the device, identifies the issue and gives a quotation.

evidence.quote: The device is sent straight to the Revibe Repair Partner — the original seller doesn't see the claim. The partner inspects the device, identifies the issue and gives a quotation.

steps.screen: Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs, QUOTATION
steps.action: Quotation: the repairer enters the price (Seller quotation). The Revibe agent reviews it (Seller quotation review). If the agent does not approve, it goes back to quotation; if approved, a cost check follows.

evidence.quote: Seller quotation → repairer enters the price → Seller quotation review → Revibe agent approves? No → back to quotation · Yes → cost check

steps.screen: Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs, box ≤ 1,500 AED
steps.action: If the cost is up to 1,500 AED, Revibe covers the repair: Ready for repair, Under repair, Repair finished, To ship back, Ship back under collection, Shipped back, Delivered. The extended warranty is consumed after the repair.

evidence.quote: ≤ 1,500 AED. Revibe covers the repair. Ready for repair → Under repair → Repair finished → To ship back → Ship back under collection → Shipped back → Delivered. The extended warranty is consumed after the repair.

steps.screen: Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs, box > 1,500 AED
steps.action: If the cost is above 1,500 AED, the customer pays the difference (cost minus 1,500 AED) and the claim shows Pending customer payment. If paid, the repair goes ahead with the same stages as ≤ 1,500 AED. If not paid, there is no repair, the device is shipped back to the customer, and RC+ is cancelled.

evidence.quote: > 1,500 AED. Customer pays the difference. Pending customer payment — customer pays (cost − 1,500 AED). Paid → repair goes ahead, same stages as ≤ 1,500 AED. Not paid → no repair · device shipped back to the customer · RC+ cancelled

steps.screen: Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs, footer
steps.action: Delivery failed on ship-back: the agent offers a new attempt; if refused, the device is disposed.

evidence.quote: Delivery failed on ship-back: agent offers a new attempt · refused → device disposed.

terms.meaning: Seller decision that the claim is repaired by the original seller: the seller repairs and ships the device back.
Seller decision that the claim is not valid; requires reason and proof, and Revibe reviews it.
Claim status once the courier delivers the device to the seller; the seller then marks it Valid or Invalid.
Revibe Care+ (RC+): covers repairs up to 1,500 AED, and Revibe pays the repair. The page 3 title for this workflow is Paid Repairs.
Repairer used after 1 year or when the customer declares misuse; the original seller does not see the claim.
Shipment document named on the page for pickup, new attempts and ship-back; the page says who creates it per market and does not expand the acronym.
Lab verification step after an Invalid claim is reviewed by Revibe; available for AE only.
Named on the page as the party the seller hands the device to for lab collection in AE; a Quiqup AWB is auto-created.
Agent status for a seller-found misuse claim where the customer holds RC+; the seller then gives a quotation.
Price entered by the repairer for the repair, reviewed by the Revibe agent before the cost check.
Market codes used throughout the workflow to set different rules; the doc does not spell out what each code stands for.
Code entered once the customer has paid the ship-back shipping fee (ZA and SA after Lab Invalid).

unclear.issue: Misuse routing is ambiguous: page 1 sends claims to the Revibe Repair Partner when “misuse declared by the customer”, but page 3 Route A keeps seller-found misuse (within 1 year) with the original seller under RC+. Confirm the difference between customer-declared and seller-found misuse before relying on it.
The phrase “Seller must cover” under a challenged Invalid claim is not explained (the cost to be covered, and by whom, is not stated).
“Within 1 year” has no start date stated anywhere (purchase date, delivery date, or claim date is not specified).

The Delivery failed rule says the seller pays a new AWB (Yes → seller pays a new AWB), but for AE and ZA ship-back AWBs are created by Revibe (30 AED deducted). It is not clear whether the seller pays for a re-attempt in AE and ZA as well.
Stripe code: the doc says it is entered once the customer has paid, but does not say who enters it (the seller, the agent, or the customer).

Lab Invalid is labelled “claim closed”, yet the same branch then continues to ship-back, Delivered, Delivery failed and Device disposed. Confirm whether the claim is closed before or after the ship-back steps.
The AWB acronym and the market codes AE, ZA and SA are used without definition; the pack has no narration to explain them.
